 Dengue fever and hand, foot, and mouth disease are developing in a complicated manner in Ho Chi Minh City.
 Both dengue fever and hand, foot, and mouth disease are on the rise in Ho Chi Minh City, with over 86,500 cases and 16 deaths. Facing the risk of further spread, the city's health sector is launching a high-intensity campaign to prevent and control the outbreaks throughout the city.
 Báo Đầu tư • 02/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 The infectious disease situation in Ho Chi Minh City is becoming increasingly worrying, with dengue fever and hand, foot, and mouth disease simultaneously recording high numbers of cases, many of which are severe and fatal. The increase in these two common diseases, especially during the rainy season and in childcare facilities, highlights the need to strengthen surveillance, control of infection sources, and proactive disease prevention in the community.
 Monitoring data up to week 43 shows that Ho Chi Minh City has recorded over 42,500 cases of dengue fever, including 11 deaths. Notably, the number of cases is trending upwards again, as the rainy season weather continues to create favorable conditions for disease-transmitting mosquitoes to breed and develop. 
 Both dengue fever and hand, foot, and mouth disease are on the rise in Ho Chi Minh City. 
 At the same time, hand, foot, and mouth disease also recorded a complex situation with over 44,000 cases, an increase of over 65% compared to the same period last year. The city recorded 5 deaths and more than 1,600 outbreaks, indicating that the risk of spread remains, especially in areas with a high concentration of young children.
 One of the factors causing concern in the healthcare sector is the circulation of Enterovirus 71 (EV71), a strain of virus capable of causing serious neurological, cardiovascular, and respiratory complications in children with hand, foot, and mouth disease. Meanwhile, the number of cases appearing in preschools and kindergartens is on the rise, increasing the risk of transmission in group settings.
 Given these developments, the Ho Chi Minh City health sector has determined that controlling both diseases simultaneously is an urgent task, requiring the participation of local authorities, healthcare facilities, schools, and individual households.
 The leaders of the Ho Chi Minh City Department of Health stated that the figures on cases and deaths serve as a warning regarding epidemic prevention and control efforts. Local authorities and the public need to increase vigilance, avoiding complacency or delays in detecting and addressing the risk of infection.
 In addition, untreated mosquito breeding grounds, unsanitary living environments, or cases of disease that go undetected can all increase the risk of disease outbreaks spreading in the community.
 For dengue fever, prevention efforts should focus on controlling disease vectors, eliminating mosquito breeding grounds, and early detection of infected individuals. For hand, foot, and mouth disease, close monitoring in schools, preschools, and daycare centers is crucial to limit the risk of outbreaks.
 You may also like Faced with the simultaneous increase in two diseases, the Ho Chi Minh City Department of Health, in coordination with the People's Committee of Di An Ward, launched a high-intensity campaign to prevent and control dengue fever and hand, foot, and mouth disease, focusing on mobilizing the participation of the political system and the people in controlling risk factors.
 During the campaign, local authorities were instructed to strengthen guidance and organize comprehensive environmental sanitation, and to review and address areas at risk of disease outbreaks. Specific responsibilities were assigned, coupled with increased inspection and supervision to ensure that disease prevention measures were implemented regularly and effectively.
 The health sector continues to strengthen epidemiological surveillance, early detection of cases, timely handling of outbreaks, and guidance for the public on recognizing warning signs of severe illness. Communication efforts are also emphasized to raise awareness of disease prevention, reduce self-treatment, and minimize delays in bringing patients to medical facilities.
 Specifically, the Ho Chi Minh City Department of Health requires that mosquito control spraying must be carried out according to professional indications, targeting the correct insects and following proper technical procedures. Local authorities are prohibited from spraying chemicals indiscriminately or considering this measure as a substitute for eliminating mosquito larvae and removing water containers that pose a breeding ground for mosquitoes.
 For hand, foot, and mouth disease, preschools and daycare centers need to strengthen daily health monitoring of children, strictly implement hygiene measures for classrooms, toys, equipment, and frequently touched surfaces. Coordination between schools and parents must be maintained to promptly detect children showing suspected symptoms and minimize the risk of cross-infection.
 In parallel with the activities of the health sector, a network of community health collaborators is mobilized to go directly to each household, lodging area, and construction site to disseminate information, provide guidance on environmental hygiene, address stagnant water sources, and implement disease prevention measures.
 The Department of Health leaders urged each family to take time at least once a week to inspect, rinse, and cover water containers, remove discarded items that could collect water, and proactively eliminate mosquito larvae. In addition, people should maintain the habit of washing hands with soap, cleaning children's toys and household items, and limiting contact with sources of infection.
 Regarding proactive disease prevention measures, Dr. Le Thi Giao Thi from Long Chau Pharmacy and Vaccination System stated that, in addition to environmental hygiene, controlling sources of infection, and early symptom detection, vaccination is a crucial solution to reduce the risk of disease and dangerous complications. Especially in the context of the simultaneous increase in dengue fever and hand, foot, and mouth disease, proactively immunizing appropriate target groups is even more significant in protecting public health.
 For dengue fever, Vietnam has now implemented the Qdenga vaccine, which is indicated for people aged 4 years and older, with a two-dose regimen administered 3 months apart.
 You may also like The vaccine was developed to prevent disease caused by all four types of Dengue virus, contributing to a reduction in the risk of illness and hospitalization. It is important to note that people who have had dengue fever are still at risk of reinfection by other types of the virus; therefore, appropriate vaccination advice is necessary, rather than assuming that having had the disease provides long-lasting immunity.
 With regard to hand, foot, and mouth disease, Vietnam's approval of the Envacgen vaccine against the EV71 virus in 2026 has opened up another preventive option for young children.
 This virus strain can cause serious complications such as encephalitis, myocarditis, and acute pulmonary edema. The vaccine is indicated for children from 2 months to under 6 years old, helping to prevent disease caused by EV71. However, because hand, foot, and mouth disease is associated with many other virus strains, vaccination cannot replace personal hygiene measures, disinfecting toys and classrooms, and monitoring children's health daily.
 Experts advise parents to proactively seek information, take their children for screening, and ensure they receive vaccinations at the appropriate age and with the correct dosage as recommended by medical professionals. The combination of vaccination, source control, and early detection of severe symptoms will help reduce the risk of hospitalization, complications, and death from these two increasingly prevalent infectious diseases.
